transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started on the Friday rail transfer plan. We have four containers — C-1 through C-4 — all inspected and accepted by the rail carrier. We need to assign the battery modules, packaged lubricants, clinic coolers, and boxed repair parts to those containers and work out any handling controls before we sign the manifest. Loading starts at 0800 and the carrier accepts the completed load at 1600. Who wants to walk us through the shipment categories first?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something critical before we go further on container assignments. I confirmed this morning in the supplier's packing certificate that the battery modules require a vented, grounded container and must be assigned to C-2. The certificate hasn't been attached to the consolidated manifest yet, but the requirement is firm.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to get something on the record before we lock in container assignments. I received an updated shop packaging sheet yesterday that hasn't been entered into the movement-control worksheet yet. The packaged lubricants must be kept in the liquid-segregation container C-3, and they cannot be loaded with clinic or battery cargo. So that's a firm constraint we need to factor in alongside Capt. Morgan's battery requirement for C-2.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to get a critical requirement on the record before we finalize container assignments. I received the clinic shipping instruction from the medical warehouse this morning — the clinic coolers require continuous refrigeration and must use C-1, with shore power connected and verified by 0700 Friday. The instruction is still being checked against the clinic's dispatch list, but the requirement is firm.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to get a critical requirement on the record before we finalize container assignments. I confirmed the scale reading at the yard this afternoon — the boxed repair parts have a combined pallet weight of exactly 1,800 kilograms and must use C-4 because the pallets need to be axle-balanced during loading. The amended weight note hasn't been added to the signed movement packet yet, but the requirement is firm.
